summary.text: Edward Braunstein is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 26 in Northeast Queens. He was born and raised in Bayside, worked as a legislative assistant in the Assembly Speaker's New York City office, and was first elected to the Assembly in 2010. He chairs the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee and is seeking re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Bayside, Queens; according to his official Assembly biography, he lives in Bay Terrace with his wife, Stephanie, and their three children.
Earned a B.S. in Finance from the State University of New York at Albany in 2003 and a J.D. from New York Law School in 2008; his Assembly biography says he passed the bar exam in February 2009.

Before his election, worked as a legislative assistant in the Assembly Speaker's New York City office (Ballotpedia names the Speaker as Sheldon Silver) and served on Community Board 11, which covers Northeast Queens neighborhoods.
Elected to the New York State Assembly in 2010 to represent the 26th District in Northeast Queens, and took office in 2011.

Chairs the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee (2025-2026) and serves on the Health, Judiciary, Rules and Ways and Means committees; chaired the Cities Committee from 2019 through 2024.
His Assembly biography says his first bill to be signed into law, banning so-called "bath salts," was enacted in July 2011 (Chapter 130 of 2011).

According to the same biography, he also sponsored laws making the unlicensed practice of law a felony (Chapter 492 of 2012), requiring campuses to notify local law enforcement of on-campus violent crimes and missing persons (Chapter 486 of 2014), and establishing the crime of unlawful dissemination or publication of an intimate image (Chapter 109 of 2019).
